modules.title: Introduction to Contemporary Nigeria
modules.html:
Nigeria's economy, challenges and democratic development since 1999. This section covers introduction to contemporary nigeria.

Key points

  • The 'Long Juju' of Arochukwu served as _____ in the pre-colonial Eastern Nigeria. — a supreme judicial oracle.
  • The Clifford Constitution of 1922 was notable for introducing the _____ in Nigeria. — elective principle.
  • The first indigenous Governor-General of Nigeria was _____. — Nnamdi Azikiwe.
  • The main objective of the 19th-century Christian missions in Nigeria was _____. — to evangelize and introduce 'civilization' through education.
  • Nigeria's first Prime Minister was _____. — Abubakar Tafawa Balewa.

Worked examples

Q: The 'Long Juju' of Arochukwu served as _____ in the pre-colonial Eastern Nigeria.
A: a supreme judicial oracle — The Long Juju (Ibini Ukpabi) oracle allowed the Aro people to dominate trade and settle disputes across Igboland and beyond.

Q: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 was notable for introducing the _____ in Nigeria.
A: elective principle — For the first time in British West Africa, the Clifford Constitution allowed for the election of representatives into the Legislative Council.

quiz.q: The 'Long Juju' of Arochukwu served as _____ in the pre-colonial Eastern Nigeria.
options: a military fort
a supreme judicial oracle
a market square
a training school for chiefs
quiz.solution: The Long Juju (Ibini Ukpabi) oracle allowed the Aro people to dominate trade and settle disputes across Igboland and beyond.

quiz.q: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 was notable for introducing the _____ in Nigeria.
options: federal system
elective principle
ministerial system
unicameral legislature
quiz.solution: For the first time in British West Africa, the Clifford Constitution allowed for the election of representatives into the Legislative Council.

quiz.q: The first indigenous Governor-General of Nigeria was _____.
options: Ahmadu Bello
Nnamdi Azikiwe
Obafemi Awolowo
Abubakar Tafawa Balewa
quiz.solution: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe took over from Sir James Robertson in 1960 as Governor-General, representing the Queen.

quiz.q: The main objective of the 19th-century Christian missions in Nigeria was _____.
options: to support British military
to evangelize and introduce 'civilization' through education
to hunt for gold
to build factories
quiz.solution: Missionaries like the CMS and Hope Waddell aimed to convert Africans and promote western education as part of the 'Bible and Plough' policy.

quiz.q: Nigeria's first Prime Minister was _____.
options: Nnamdi Azikiwe
Ahmadu Bello
Abubakar Tafawa Balewa
Obafemi Awolowo
quiz.solution: Balewa, from the NPC, led the government at the center from 1957 until the 1966 coup.

quiz.q: The 'Operation Wetie' in Western Nigeria (1965) was a period of _____.
options: agricultural boom
political violence and arson
massive rainfall
religious revival
quiz.solution: Following the rigged Western Region elections of 1965, widespread violence broke out where political opponents were doused in petrol and set ablaze.

quiz.q: The first capital of Nigeria was _____.
options: Abuja
Calabar
Lagos
Lokoja
quiz.solution: Lagos served as the seat of government from the colonial era until the capital was moved to Abuja in 1991.

quiz.q: The first University College in Nigeria was established in 1948 at _____.
options: Lagos
Nsukka
Ibadan
Zaria
quiz.solution: The University College, Ibadan (initially affiliated with the University of London) was the premier higher education institution in Nigeria.

quiz.q: The Richards Constitution of 1946 was significant for introducing _____ into Nigeria.
options: Direct taxation
Federalism
Regionalism
Universal Suffrage
quiz.solution: The Richards Constitution divided Nigeria into three regions (North, West, and East), laying the path for regional politics.

quiz.q: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) was formed in 1975 under the leadership of Nigeria and _____.
options: Ghana
Togo
Senegal
Ivory Coast
quiz.solution: Nigeria (Gowon) and Togo (Eyadema) were the primary architects of ECOWAS.

quiz.q: The first capital of the Nigeria Colony after the 1914 amalgamation was _____.
options: Lokoja
Lagos
Calabar
Kaduna
quiz.solution: Lagos remained the capital of amalgamated Nigeria until the move to Abuja in 1991.

quiz.q: The Amalgamation of Northern and Southern Nigeria occurred in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: 1914.

quiz.q: The first Prime Minister of Nigeria was:
options: Tafawa Balewa
Nnamdi Azikiwe
Obafemi Awolowo
Herbert Macaulay
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Tafawa Balewa.

quiz.q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Nigeria?
options: Nnamdi Azikiwe
Abubakar Tafawa Balewa
Obafemi Awolowo
Ahmadu Bello
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Abubakar Tafawa Balewa.

quiz.q: The Richards Constitution divided Nigeria into:
options: Three regions
Four regions
Twelve states
36 states
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Three regions.

quiz.q: The capital of Nigeria moved from Lagos to Abuja in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: 1991.

quiz.q: The earliest known culture in Nigeria, famous for its terracotta sculptures, is the...
options: Ife Culture
Nok Culture
Benin Culture
Igbo-Ukwu Culture
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Nok Culture.

quiz.q: The archaeological site in eastern Nigeria famous for its advanced bronze casting is...
options: Oyo-Ile
Igbo-Ukwu
Taruga
Daima
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Igbo-Ukwu.

quiz.q: The protectorates of Northern and Southern Nigeria were amalgamated in...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: 1914.

quiz.q: The 1946 Richards Constitution divided Nigeria into...
options: Two regions
Three regions
Twelve states
Four provinces
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Three regions.

quiz.q: The capital of Nigeria was moved from Lagos to Abuja in...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: 1991.

quiz.q: Nigeria's membership in the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) began in...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: 1971.

quiz.q: The protectorate of Southern Nigeria was created in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: 1900.

quiz.q: The Amalgamation of Northern and Southern Nigeria took place in:
quiz.solution: Past question (WAEC 2025). Correct answer: 1914.

quiz.q: The first census in Nigeria was in:
quiz.solution: Past question (WAEC 2025). Correct answer: 1952/53.

quiz.q: The Oyo Empire reached its peak of power under the administrative system of checks and balances involving the Alaafin and the...
options: Ogboni
Oyo Mesi
Ese
Iwarefa
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Oyo Mesi.

quiz.q: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 was significant because it introduced...
options: Independence
A central Legislative Council and Regional Houses
Military rule
The Pound Sterling
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: A central Legislative Council and Regional Houses.

quiz.q: Which empire was known as the 'Land of Gold'?
options: Ghana Empire
Mali Empire
Songhai Empire
Benin Empire
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Ghana Empire.

quiz.q: Nana of Itsekiri was deported by the British in:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: 1894.

quiz.q: The Aro Confederacy was in:
options: Eastern Nigeria
Western Nigeria
Northern Nigeria
Middle Belt
quiz.solution: Past question (WAEC 2025). Correct answer: Eastern Nigeria.
